cues.en: The most important thing to recognize about color is that it doesn't actually
cues.zh: 关于颜色，最重要的一点是要认识到，它其实并不

cues.en: exist.
cues.zh: 存在。

cues.en: It's true. Electromagnetic energy exists all around you, and if we sort it by wavelength, your vision is sensitive to a small sliver of that spectrum. But the sliver isn't literally filled with the vibrant hues shown in diagrams, it's just the waves. And you don't sense all of them with one organ. The back of a typical human eye is peppered with four kinds of photoreceptors.
cues.zh: 确实如此。电磁能量充满你的四周，如果按波长排序，你的视觉只对其中一小段光谱敏感。但这一小段里并没有示意图上那种鲜艳的色彩，只有波。而且你不是靠一个器官感知所有波。典型人眼的后部密布着四种光感受器。

cues.en: One kind, the rods, is for seeing in low light and doesn't matter right now, but the other three, the cones,
cues.zh: 其中一种叫视杆细胞，负责弱光视觉，现在先不管；另外三种叫视锥细胞，

cues.en: specialize in being sensitive to long, medium, and short wavelengths of light. The sorts of wavelengths that tend to bounce off stuff that is all over Earth.
cues.zh: 专门对长、中、短波长的光敏感。这些波长往往会从地球上各种东西上反射回来。

cues.en: How convenient.
cues.zh: 真方便。

cues.en: There is a lot of overlap between these three sensitivities.
cues.zh: 这三种敏感度之间有很大重叠。

cues.en: In fact, it's impossible to perceive the pure signal from just one type of cones. All visual information that gets to the brain is a combination of at least two. These combinations feel like different hues spanning every frequency of the visible spectrum.
cues.zh: 事实上，不可能只靠一种视锥细胞感知到纯信号。到达大脑的所有视觉信息，都是至少两种视锥细胞信号的组合。这些组合让我们感受到覆盖整个可见光谱的不同色调。

cues.en: That's a pretty dicey method for telling things apart if you think about it. I mean, when you see orange light, you might be looking at a single source emitting waves of that frequency,
cues.zh: 仔细想想，用这种方法区分事物挺不靠谱的。我是说，当你看到橙光时，可能看到的是一个单一光源发出该频率的波，

cues.en: or you might be looking at multiple sources emitting multiple frequencies that combine to stimulate your cones in the exact same way. The eye can't tell the difference. You can even perceive a combination of opposite ends
cues.zh: 也可能看到多个光源发出多种频率，它们组合起来，以完全相同的方式刺激你的视锥细胞。眼睛分辨不出区别。你甚至能把光谱相反两端的组合

cues.en: spectrum as a hue. Purple and magenta don't exist at any individual frequency but are a mix of the longest and shortest visible waves.
cues.zh: 感知为一种色调。紫色和洋红色并不存在于任何单一频率，而是最长和最短可见波的混合。

cues.en: It's all a three-dimensional
cues.zh: 它其实是一个三维的

cues.en: blob of perception possibilities.
cues.zh: 感知可能性团块。

cues.en: Or if you wanna be fancy about it and use math, a spectrum locus plotted inside the cone excitation space,
cues.zh: 或者如果你想说得花哨点、用数学来讲，就是在视锥激发空间中绘制的光谱轨迹，

cues.en: or if you average out the dimension of brightness,
cues.zh: 或者如果你把亮度这个维度平均掉，

cues.en: a melty triangle of all observable hues. Every color is an imbalance between the three cone outputs. The more balanced there is, the less saturated a color seems until proportionally
cues.zh: 就是所有可观察色相组成的融化三角形。每种颜色都是三种视锥输出之间的不平衡。输出越平衡，颜色看起来就越不饱和，直到按比例

cues.en: equal outputs just look like no color at all.
cues.zh: 相等的输出看起来就像完全没有颜色。

cues.en: Remember, this whole chromaticity diagram is just what happens in your head.
cues.zh: 记住，这整个色度图不过是你大脑里发生的事。

cues.en: For people with atypical color perception or other animals,
cues.zh: 对于色彩感知非典型的人或其他动物来说，

cues.en: the diagram might be shaped differently and filled with different values, but it's just as valid an interpretation of the achromatic energy hell that is the real world.
cues.zh: 这张图的形状可能不同，填的值也不同，但它同样是对现实世界这个无彩色能量地狱的有效解读。

cues.en: And let's not discriminate against machines either. Display devices and print mediums all have their own, usually more limited color gamuts. You're watching this as a Rec seven zero nine image displayed in the modest sRGB
cues.zh: 也别歧视机器。显示设备和印刷媒介都有各自的色域，通常还更有限。你现在看到的是一张 Rec 709 图像，显示在普通的 sRGB

cues.en: color space, but that's okay. A limited palette works fine as long as the color relationships remain the same. That's why things don't seem too weird in different lighting environments,
cues.zh: 色彩空间里，但没关系。只要颜色关系保持不变，有限的调色板也完全够用。这就是为什么在不同光照环境下，东西看起来不会太怪，

cues.en: and also why it's okay to simplify the chromaticity diagram into a circle. The hue circle, with all its pleasing color geometry,

cues.en: works because it's an abstraction of human vision itself.

And a century and a half after that, we still use Newton's hue circle as a standard visual aid for additive color relationships.
cues.zh: 一个半世纪后，James Clerk Maxwell 弄清了电磁波谱，并阐述了三色分离原理，这几乎成了所有彩色成像技术的基础。又过了一个半世纪，我们仍把 Newton 的色相环当作说明加色关系的标准直观工具。

cues.en: It's handy for figuring out effective color palettes in digital art and for performing intricate color grading on moving images.

cues.en: Here, the goal is to push the relatively limited color space to somehow convey the depths of human visual experience and imagination.
cues.zh: 这里的目标是让相对有限的色彩空间，设法传达人类视觉体验和想象力的深度。

cues.en: To do this right, we need to inform our perceptions with reliable measuring instruments,
cues.zh: 要做好这一点，我们需要用可靠的测量工具来校准感知，

cues.en: mainly a vectorscope and waveform monitor. These used to be expensive dedicated pieces of hardware, but now they're just a click away in all your favorite video editing applications.
cues.zh: 主要是矢量示波器和波形监视器。它们过去是昂贵的专用硬件，如今在你常用的视频剪辑软件里一键就能调用。

cues.en: The vectorscope plots where the colors of your image fall in terms of hue and saturation on the hue circle. Neutral tones not sitting in the middle? Pull them over. Neon lights oversaturated?
cues.zh: 矢量示波器会在色相环上标出图像中颜色的色相和饱和度位置。中性色调不在正中间？把它们拉过去。霓虹灯过饱和了？

You're designed to prioritize contrast way over color.

cues.en: and why color blindness is not really a big deal. Many people with color deficiency in their vision don't even realize they have it until later in life. And in this fascinating art experiment, painter Marco Bucci demonstrates how almost completely random colors can look sensible in paintings with well defined black and white tones.
cues.zh: 也是色盲其实没什么大不了的原因。许多有色觉缺陷的人直到晚年才意识到自己有这个问题。而在这个引人入胜的艺术实验里，画家 Marco Bucci 展示了：在黑白明暗关系清晰的作品中，几乎完全随机的颜色也能显得协调。
